# Interpolation models

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_docs.py from the model cards; do not edit. -->

10 interpolation models. Each section says what the model is, whether it may be used commercially and how fast it is; licences and checks are under Details.

Input: two RGB images (consecutive frames). Output: the frame between them at `timestep` (0.5 by default; 0 = the first, 1 = the second), RGB in [0, 1].

Measured on RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130; `fastforks bench MODEL --size HxW` measures yours. The summary uses one input, 1080x1920: kernels time with its speed-up over the faster original run, and kernels peak reserved memory with its ratio to the smaller original one. Where measured (one variant per family), a variant's table also lists portable under `torch.compile` and the fp16 TensorRT engine of portable ([export](../export.md); memory: the engine's device memory + torch's peak). – = not measured; no kernels = the family has no kernels backend (reason under its table). Reserved memory is the allocator's cache: kernels (CUDA graphs, cuDNN workspaces) can reserve a few percent to some tens of percent more than portable at the same allocated peak.

Other devices: [Apple M1 Pro 16 GB](../devices/apple-m1-pro-16gb.md), [Apple M1 Pro 16 GB (MLX)](../devices/apple-m1-pro-mlx-16gb.md), [NVIDIA L4](../devices/l4-22gb.md), [NVIDIA L40S](../devices/l40s-44gb.md), [NVIDIA A10](../devices/a10-22gb.md), [NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB](../devices/a100-sxm4-40gb.md), [NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000](../devices/rtx-pro-6000-96gb.md); [across devices](../benchmarks.md#other-devices).

## EMA-VFI

EMA-VFI (Zhang et al., CVPR 2023; large and small, for the middle frame or any time): makes the frame between two video frames from motion and appearance features that inter-frame attention extracts together, for slow motion and higher frame rates. Apache-2.0 code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ema-vfi` | synthetic (1080x1920) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 296<br>233<br>185<br>165<br>124 | 3940 / 4290<br>1659 / 2082<br>1659 / 2102<br>3325 / 3542<br>1719 / 1786 |

| `ema-vfi-t` | synthetic (1080x1920) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 287<br>233<br>207<br>165<br>125 | 3940 / 4290<br>2827 / 3184<br>368 / 3566<br>3325 / 3702<br>1719 / 1766 |

## FILM

FILM (Reda et al., Google, ECCV 2022): makes the middle frame between two video frames, also for large motion, from a flow pyramid in both directions and features shared across scales. Apache-2.0 code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `film` | synthetic (1080x1920) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 464<br>412<br>328<br>332<br>189 | 2953 / 3556<br>2397 / 2702<br>2397 / 2942<br>2666 / 3192<br>2658 / 2658 |

## GIMM-VFI

GIMM-VFI (GIMM-VFI-R and its perceptual GIMM-VFI-R-P, Guo et al., NeurIPS 2024): makes the frame at any time between two video frames from a learned continuous motion field (RAFT flow), for slow motion and higher frame rates. Non-commercial code and weights (S-Lab License 1.0).

Commercial use: **no** (code: LicenseRef-noncommercial (noncommercial); weights: LicenseRef-noncommercial).

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |

| `gimm-vfi-r-p` | synthetic (1080x1920) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | OOM<br>2528<br>1520<br>1498<br>fails: TensorRT parser: Sc node | –<br>5394 / 6518<br>4511 / 5282<br>12051 / 12880<br>– |

### Limitations

- At 480 x 854 the standalone GIMM-VFI-R FP32 TensorRT engine returned different frames from portable FP32. Mean normalized absolute pixel error was 0.07687. The same ONNX file run in ONNX Runtime measured 0.000029.
- At 480 x 854 the FP32 GIMM-VFI-R-P TensorRT encoders took 1190 ms versus 1231 ms for paired portable FP32. Estimated peak allocated memory was 3592 MiB versus 3282 MiB. The speed table also includes the faster FP16 modes.
- The GIMM-VFI-R feature encoder alone passed the 16-triplet check. End-to-end FP32 latency was 1210 ms versus 1230 ms for paired portable FP32, with a PSNR change of at most 0.0395 dB on the checked triplets.

## RIFE

RIFE (Practical-RIFE 4.25, 4.26 and 4.25 lite, Huang et al.): makes the frame between two video frames from the optical flow it estimates between them, for slow motion and higher frame rates. MIT code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|

### Measured

DAVIS 2017 trainval 480p (JPEG), frames 0 / 2 and 20 / 22 of each of the 90 videos give the frame 1 / 21 at time 0.5, compared with the real one: PSNR and SSIM (Gaussian 11 x 11, sigma 1.5) of the output rounded to uint8, on RGB in [0, 1], averaged over the triplets for the 180-triplet benchmark. The fixed-shape comparison uses all 172 triplets at the native 480 x 854 size and follows the same scoring protocol. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.
